candidate_1: The **base-rate fallacy** occurs when someone neglects how common an event is overall and overweights vivid or case-specific evidence. Political examples: (1) using one shocking immigrant-crime story to imply immigrants generally have high crime rates without population-adjusted data; (2) citing a rare vaccine injury while ignoring the baseline risks of disease; (3) presenting one fraudulent ballot as evidence that election fraud is widespread; (4) showcasing one failed clean-energy project to condemn the sector without comparing failure rates; (5) highlighting one wealthy welfare recipient to characterize all beneficiaries. The claim may be true or false; the fallacy is the missing denominator and comparison group.
